paragraphs.text: translated by
1. Now all my other friends are here assembled: my Sire-in-law alone hath not come hither.
paragraphs.original: विश्वो ह्यन्यो अरिराजगाम ममेदह श्वशुरो ना जगाम ।
paragraphs.translit: viśvo hyanyo arirājagāma mamedaha śvaśuro nā jagāma |

paragraphs.text: So might he eat the grain and drink the Soma, and, satisfied, return unto; his dwelling.
paragraphs.original: जक्षीयाद्धाना उत सोमं पपीयात्स्वाशितः पुनरस्तं जगायात्
paragraphs.translit: jakṣīyāddhānā uta somaṃ papīyātsvāśitaḥ punarastaṃ jagāyāt

paragraphs.text: 2. Loud belloweth the Bull whose horns are sharpened: upon the height above earth's breadth he standeth.
paragraphs.original: स रोरुवद्वृषभस्तिग्मशृङ्गो वर्ष्मन्तस्थौ वरिमन्ना पृथिव्याः ।
paragraphs.translit: sa roruvadvṛṣabhastigmaśṛṅgo varṣmantasthau varimannā pṛthivyāḥ |

paragraphs.text: That man I guard and save in all his troubles who fills my flanks when he hath shed the Soma.
paragraphs.original: विश्वेष्वेनं वृजनेषु पामि यो मे कुक्षी सुतसोमः पृणाति
paragraphs.translit: viśveṣvenaṃ vṛjaneṣu pāmi yo me kukṣī sutasomaḥ pṛṇāti

paragraphs.text: 3. Men with the stone press out for thee, O Indra, strong, gladdening Soma, and thereof thou drinkest.
paragraphs.original: अद्रिणा ते मन्दिन इन्द्र तूयान्सुन्वन्ति सोमान्पिबसि त्वमेषाम् ।
paragraphs.translit: adriṇā te mandina indra tūyānsunvanti somānpibasi tvameṣām |

paragraphs.text: Bulls they dress for thee, and of these thou eatest when, Maghavan, with food thou art invited.
paragraphs.original: पचन्ति ते वृषभाँ अत्सि तेषां पृक्षेण यन्मघवन्हूयमानः
paragraphs.translit: pacanti te vṛṣabhām̐ atsi teṣāṃ pṛkṣeṇa yanmaghavanhūyamānaḥ

paragraphs.text: 4. Resolve for me, O singer, this my riddle: The rivers send their swelling water backward:
paragraphs.original: इदं सु मे जरितरा चिकिद्धि प्रतीपं शापं नद्यो वहन्ति ।
paragraphs.translit: idaṃ su me jaritarā cikiddhi pratīpaṃ śāpaṃ nadyo vahanti |

paragraphs.text: The fox steals up to the approaching lion: the jackal drives the wild-boar from the brushwood.
paragraphs.original: लोपाशः सिंहं प्रत्यञ्चमत्साः क्रोष्टा वराहं निरतक्त कक्षात्
paragraphs.translit: lopāśaḥ siṃhaṃ pratyañcamatsāḥ kroṣṭā varāhaṃ niratakta kakṣāt

paragraphs.text: 5. How shall I solve this riddle, I, the simple, declare the thought of thee the Wise and Mighty?
paragraphs.original: कथा त एतदहमा चिकेतं गृत्सस्य पाकस्तवसो मनीषाम् ।
paragraphs.translit: kathā ta etadahamā ciketaṃ gṛtsasya pākastavaso manīṣām |

paragraphs.text: Tell us, well knowing, as befits the season: Whitherward is thy prosperous car advancing?
paragraphs.original: त्वं नो विद्वाँ ऋतुथा वि वोचो यमर्धं ते मघवन्क्षेम्या धूः
paragraphs.translit: tvaṃ no vidvām̐ ṛtuthā vi voco yamardhaṃ te maghavankṣemyā dhūḥ

paragraphs.text: 6. Thus do they magnify me, me the mighty higher than even high heaven is my car-pole.
paragraphs.original: एवा हि मां तवसं वर्धयन्ति दिवश्चिन्मे बृहत उत्तरा धूः ।
paragraphs.translit: evā hi māṃ tavasaṃ vardhayanti divaścinme bṛhata uttarā dhūḥ |

paragraphs.text: I all at once demolish many thousands: my Sire begot me with no foe to match me.
paragraphs.original: पुरू सहस्रा नि शिशामि साकमशत्रुं हि मा जनिता जजान
paragraphs.translit: purū sahasrā ni śiśāmi sākamaśatruṃ hi mā janitā jajāna

paragraphs.text: 7. Yea, and the Gods have known me also, Indra, as mighty, fierce and strong in every exploit.
paragraphs.original: एवा हि मां तवसं जज्ञुरुग्रं कर्मन्कर्मन्वृषणमिन्द्र देवाः ।
paragraphs.translit: evā hi māṃ tavasaṃ jajñurugraṃ karmankarmanvṛṣaṇamindra devāḥ |

paragraphs.text: Exulting with the bolt I slaughtered Vrtra, and for the offerer open with might the cow-stall.
paragraphs.original: वधीं वृत्रं वज्रेण मन्दसानोऽप व्रजं महिना दाशुषे वम्
paragraphs.translit: vadhīṃ vṛtraṃ vajreṇa mandasāno'pa vrajaṃ mahinā dāśuṣe vam

paragraphs.text: 8. The Deities approached, they carried axes; splitting the wood they came with their attendants.
paragraphs.original: देवास आयन्परशूँरबिभ्रन्वना वृश्चन्तो अभि विड्भिरायन् ।
paragraphs.translit: devāsa āyanparaśūm̐rabibhranvanā vṛścanto abhi viḍbhirāyan |

paragraphs.text: They laid good timber in the fire-receivers, and burnt the grass up where they found it growing.
paragraphs.original: नि सुद्र्वं दधतो वक्षणासु यत्रा कृपीटमनु तद्दहन्ति
paragraphs.translit: ni sudrvaṃ dadhato vakṣaṇāsu yatrā kṛpīṭamanu taddahanti

paragraphs.text: 9. The hare hath swallowed up the opposing razor: I sundered with a clod the distant mountain.
paragraphs.original: शशः क्षुरं प्रत्यञ्चं जगाराद्रिं लोगेन व्यभेदमारात् ।
paragraphs.translit: śaśaḥ kṣuraṃ pratyañcaṃ jagārādriṃ logena vyabhedamārāt |

paragraphs.text: The great will I make subject to the little: the calf shall wax in strength and cat the bullock.
paragraphs.original: बृहन्तं चिदृहते रन्धयानि वयद्वत्सो वृषभं शूशुवानः
paragraphs.translit: bṛhantaṃ cidṛhate randhayāni vayadvatso vṛṣabhaṃ śūśuvānaḥ

paragraphs.text: 10. There hath the strong-winged eagle left his talon, as a snared lion leaves the trap that caught him.
paragraphs.original: सुपर्ण इत्था नखमा सिषायावरुद्धः परिपदं न सिंहः ।
paragraphs.translit: suparṇa itthā nakhamā siṣāyāvaruddhaḥ paripadaṃ na siṃhaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Even the wild steer in his thirst is captured: the leather strap still holds his foot entangled.
paragraphs.original: निरुद्धश्चिन्महिषस्तर्ष्यावान्गोधा तस्मा अयथं कर्षदेतत्
paragraphs.translit: niruddhaścinmahiṣastarṣyāvāngodhā tasmā ayathaṃ karṣadetat

paragraphs.text: 11. So may the leather strap their foot entangle who fatten on the viands of the Brahman.
paragraphs.original: तेभ्यो गोधा अयथं कर्षदेतद्ये ब्रह्मणः प्रतिपीयन्त्यन्नैः ।
paragraphs.translit: tebhyo godhā ayathaṃ karṣadetadye brahmaṇaḥ pratipīyantyannaiḥ |

paragraphs.text: They all devour the bulls set free to wander, while they themselves destroy their bodies' vigour.
paragraphs.original: सिम उक्ष्णोऽवसृष्टाँ अदन्ति स्वयं बलानि तन्वः शृणानाः
paragraphs.translit: sima ukṣṇo'vasṛṣṭām̐ adanti svayaṃ balāni tanvaḥ śṛṇānāḥ

paragraphs.text: 12. They were well occupied with holy duties who sped in person with their lauds to Soma.
paragraphs.original: एते शमीभिः सुशमी अभूवन्ये हिन्विरे तन्वः सोम उक्थैः ।
paragraphs.translit: ete śamībhiḥ suśamī abhūvanye hinvire tanvaḥ soma ukthaiḥ |

paragraphs.text: Speaking like man, mete to us wealth and booty: in heaven thou hast the name and fame of Hero.
paragraphs.original: नृवद्वदन्नुप नो माहि वाजान्दिवि श्रवो दधिषे नाम वीरः
paragraphs.translit: nṛvadvadannupa no māhi vājāndivi śravo dadhiṣe nāma vīraḥ
